clue.text: Delivery cost in subsequent period?

parts.note: post- is the prefix meaning after or subsequent
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A question about whether a delivery charge falls in some later period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subsequent' wants to read as an ordinary adjective, but it supplies POST, the prefix meaning 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage is the charge paid for having a letter or parcel delivered by mail.

clue.text: One in cop tale is not out of place here

definitions.text: One in cop tale is not out of place here

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the following words before they are jumbled
out of place says the letters are disordered and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Somewhere a person in a detective story would naturally turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: Put I inside COP TALE IS NOT and rearrange all thirteen letters. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the place: someone who has been arrested ('one in') in a police story belongs there.
explanation.definitionFit: A police station is where a detained suspect in a crime story naturally ends up, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Lends money to get fuel that's just below the ground

parts.note: to sub someone is to lend them money as an advance
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Someone lending cash so they can buy fuel that lies close under the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB, meaning to lend money in advance, is an informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsoil is the layer of earth lying immediately beneath the topsoil, just under the surface.

clue.text: Have the same idea about filling time

indicators.note: filling means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an age is a period of time
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Two people thinking alike about how to fill up the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to share the same opinion as someone else.

clue.text: Sending out disciple at last to church outpost

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of disciple

parts.note: a mission is a station set up by a church in a remote place

explanation.surface: A disciple finally being sent off to a remote church station.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is the act of giving off or sending out something, such as light or gas.

clue.text: Signal one can't finish large bottle

parts.note: a flag is used to signal

indicators.note: can't finish means the word one loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone signalling that they cannot finish off a big bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large bottle or vessel for wine or cider.

clue.text: Fish getting surrounded by smaller ones easily

indicators.note: getting surrounded by means the first fish sits inside the smaller ones

parts.note: fry are young, small fish
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A big fish swimming in a shoal of little fish, with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is just EEL, and 'smaller ones' are FRY, young fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Freely can mean without difficulty or hindrance, much like easily.

clue.text: Stupid person forgetting name in a very short time — one helps out

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: forgetting means the letter for name is dropped

parts.note: an instant is a very short time

explanation.surface: A fool who can't recall a name in a flash, yet someone lends a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is a person who helps another in their work.

clue.text: Where one may find sesame seeds, if having a lot of luck?

definitions.text: Where one may find sesame seeds
definitions.meaning: sesame seeds are sprinkled on top of bread rolls
an idiom for enjoying a run of success

explanation.surface: Wondering where sesame seeds turn up, if you are lucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a roll is an idiom for a winning streak, and seeds literally sit on a bread roll.

clue.text: I chance including King in series of roués

indicators.note: in places the assembled piece inside series

parts.note: a line is a series

indicators.note: including puts the king's letter inside chance

parts.note: a bet is a chance taken
R stands for Rex, king

explanation.surface: Someone gambling with royalty among a row of rakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is used as an adjective here, so 'of roués' is the definition and 'series' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Libertine as an adjective describes the dissolute, rakish behaviour typical of roués.

clue.text: Sight in sky enthralling one in part of flight

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one is held inside

parts.note: a star is seen in the night sky
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Something in the sky captivating a person on an aeroplane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel, but it means a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is one step in a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Operation at a distance, note, appearing in revolutionary electromotor

indicators.note: appearing in means the letter goes inside the rearranged motor
revolutionary means turned about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A remark about an electric motor that spins round.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote control is the operating of a machine from a distance.

clue.text: Charles I apparently an old-womanish type

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, the royal cipher of King Charles
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: King Charles the First seemingly a fussy old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles I signed as CR, Carolus Rex; read the numeral as the word ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A crone is a withered old woman, the very type of the elderly woman.

clue.text: Where to get lots of drinks in upland areas, when heading west

indicators.note: in places the drinks inside the turned uplands
heading west in an across clue means read right to left

parts.note: moors are high open uplands
ales are drinks

explanation.surface: Advice on where to find plenty to drink in the hills when travelling west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' looks like quantity, but means auction lots.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesroom is an auction room, where lots are put up for sale.

clue.text: A mixture of liquids, that's the answer

definitions.meaning: a substance dissolved in a liquid forms a homogeneous mixture
the correct result to a puzzle

explanation.surface: A chemist declaring a blend of fluids is just what is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Solution means both a liquid mixture of dissolved substances and the answer to a problem.

clue.text: Chap, one entering lake in waterproof material

indicators.note: entering means the chap and one go inside lake

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
Paul is a chap's name
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A man wading into a lake wearing waterproof cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpaulin is heavy waterproof canvas used as a cover.

clue.text: Dance round object, extremely exultant

parts.note: a ball is a round object

indicators.note: extremely picks the first and last letters of exultant

explanation.surface: Dancing joyfully around something round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet is a theatrical form of dance.

clue.text: Race is on for rewriting film treatment

indicators.note: rewriting means the words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Scriptwriters hurrying to rewrite a screenplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of a film's plot, which is what a film treatment is.

clue.text: Heavenly place draws leader of angels back

indicators.note: back means the whole piece is read in reverse

parts.note: to drag is to draw along

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of angels

explanation.surface: A celestial realm pulling the head angel backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Asgard is the home of the gods in Norse mythology.
explanation.definitionFit: Asgard is the realm of the gods in Norse myth, a heavenly abode.

clue.text: Besotted girl needing to mature that's losing weight

indicators.note: losing means the letter for weight is dropped

parts.note: to grow up is to mature
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A lovestruck girl who needs to grow up and slim down.
explanation.definitionFit: A groupie is an infatuated fan, typically a girl, who follows a band or star.

clue.text: In religious fervour, and still after church backing

indicators.note: after sends the still piece second, behind the turned church
backing means the church letters are reversed

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
static means still or motionless

explanation.surface: A worshipper in a trance staying motionless after church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In religious fervour' reads like scene-setting but is the definition; 'still' is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic can describe someone in a state of rapturous religious transport.

clue.text: Article on time in live stage productions

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: in places time inside live

parts.note: are as in 'we are', to exist or live

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about timing in live shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' is the verb to exist, not the adjective about a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre denotes stage plays and productions collectively.

clue.text: An unsuitable thing if erected in fog

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside fog

parts.note: mist is a light fog

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means set upright, read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Something unsuitable put up in the fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfit is something or someone that does not fit in or suit its surroundings.

clue.text: In a lot, so I suffer — this?

definitions.text: In a lot, so I suffer — this?

indicators.note: suffer suggests letters in distress and so rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A lonely person lamenting how much they suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of IN A LOT SO I is what the whole clue describes: being cut off makes one suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolation, being solitary, is a condition that causes much suffering, as the clue suggests.

clue.text: Honest line in the main, nothing less

indicators.note: in places line inside the shortened sea
less means the nothing letter is removed

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the sea or ocean
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A straight line out in the open sea, with nothing missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean can mean morally honest and free of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Top Conservative leading the others

indicators.note: leading puts Conservative in front

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A senior Tory heading the remaining members.
explanation.definitionFit: A crest is the summit or highest point of something.

clue.text: One palace is more than enough for this kingdom

indicators.note: the phrase says the words contain the kingdom with room to spare, so it lies within them

explanation.surface: A small Himalayan realm that needs only one royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal was a Himalayan kingdom until 2008.

clue.text: One always receptive to new brands of circus entertainment?

definitions.text: One always receptive to new brands of circus entertainment?

parts.words: One always receptive to new brands of circus entertainment?
parts.note: brands read as burning sticks, which a circus performer takes into the mouth

explanation.surface: A consumer always keen to try new brands of circus show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brands' looks like product names, but means burning torches.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-eater is a circus performer who puts flaming torches into the mouth.

clue.text: Item of fruit: just one of a miserly quantity?

definitions.meaning: a nut counts botanically as a fruit

definitions.text: just one of a miserly quantity
definitions.meaning: a paltry sum of money, so this is a single unit of it

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit as a stingy single portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is a nut, technically a fruit, and peanuts means a tiny amount of money.

clue.text: Go faster from store: given part exchange, would all go

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase swap places

parts.note: if stock would all go it would sell out

explanation.surface: Selling stock quickly with a part-exchange offer to clear it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part exchange' suggests a trade-in deal; it swaps the halves of SELL OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsell is to sell more quickly or in greater numbers than a rival product.
